text:
anya: Heads-up: saw a repro where responses start repeating tokens from previous requests after ~30k tokens in the same worker. Not a memory leak per se, looks like stale KV blocks being reused.

mike: repro steps? config? model? :eyes:

anya: long-chat test with 64k context, gpt-style decoder, seq_len distribution skewed. We hit paging/eviction a lot. Repro attached as a small harness log below.

anya: ```
[worker-42] alloc_page id=3 evict->page=7
[worker-42] store_block fp=0x7f8a1234 tag=0x9c
[worker-42] load_block fp=0x7f8a1234 tag=0x8f  # mismatch
``` 

tariq: hmm fp looks like a fingerprint value. Are we deduping by fingerprint across requests? That would explain cross-request reuse if fp collisions or stale mapping exist.

leo: we do have a fingerprint table for dedupe + fast lookup. It was supposed to be per-worker and evicted entries get tombstoned. Could be tombstone recycling bug.

anya: profiler-bot just posted heap/profile: KV pages churn spikes at the same time as the contamination. Also saw "fp_index==0" for reused frames.

profiler-bot: ```
sample: kv_entries: 120k -> 114k (-5%)
cache_hit_ratio: 0.38 -> 0.35
stale_fp_matches: 42  # new metric
cpu: > baseline by 7% during long contexts
``` 

mike: any recent changes to fingerprint calc? kernel selection or batching heuristics shouldn't affect fp but maybe the layout/offsets changed.

tariq: there was a recent patch that changed block header packing to save 8 bytes (PR #5212). It shifted token_offset stored in header from 32->24 bits and we reinterpreted the raw header in a few places. Could be sign/shift bug.

leo: spike: if token_offset is parsed wrong when we compute fp = hash(model_id, layer, token_offset, kv_len), then an entry for token_offset 0x100 becomes treated as 0x1000000 and you get misaligned matches.

anya: yep reproduced locally by flipping the offset mask. Test case:

anya: ```
# reproduce in unit test
hdr.raw = 0x112233445566
parse_offset(hdr) -> wrong
assert lookup(fp_for(parsed)) returns older_block
``` 

mike: okay patch suggestion: make fp include request_epoch_id (per-request monotonic) so cross-request reuse is impossible even if header misparse occurs. But that's bandaid; root cause still header layout mismatch.

tariq: agree. I'll add a stricter assertion in de/serialize: validate parsed token_offset + kv_len <= page_size and fail fast. That should catch corrupt parsing in CI.

leo: also add a per-worker generation counter to fingerprint key as an extra safety net. Minimal perf hit.

devops-bot: Canary gate: add rollout with 10% workers running new header parser + fp-gen. Monitoring: stale_fp_matches and cross_request_conflicts.

mike: who picks this up? tariq to triage header parse + unit test. leo to add generation counter + perf benchmark. anya to produce minimal harness and attach failing log. I'll file a short incident ticket.

anya: filed REDWOOD-INC-2026 and pushed the harness to /ci/repros/kvcache-fp-misalignment. Attaching link: https://redwood.internal/ci/repros/1979998888

tariq: starting the fix now, will post PR and link.

mike: thanks. prioritize patch + canary this week. If anyone sees dropped tokens or repetition in staging, ping @oncall immediately.

leo: note to self: add deterministic fuzz to header encode/decode in nightly to catch layout regressions.

profiler-bot: monitoring rule created: alert if stale_fp_matches > 5/min on any worker for 1m.

anya: great. I'll follow up after canary and run long-context stress overnight.
